headline: Whether the Gold Rewards Card's +0.025% stacks on top of the EcoCard bonus is ambiguous in the docs, so the $140.00 correction is one of two defensible answers.

issues.summary: The Gold Rewards Card's 0.025% appears twice. doc_013 calls it a relationship bonus on top of the base rate, and doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_045 says credit card bonuses DO stack with relationship bonuses; doc_014 and doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_045's own example list the same 0.025% as a credit card bonus that loses to EcoCard. The gold drops it (EcoCard 0.6% only).
evidence: doc_savings_accounts_gold_account_013: "you receive an additional 0.025% relationship bonus APY on top of the base rate"
doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_045: "credit card APY bonuses DO stack with other types of bonuses, such as: ... Relationship bonuses for holding multiple Rho-Bank products"

doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_045 example: "Gold Rewards Card: +0.025% APY bonus / Platinum Rewards Card: +0.15% APY bonus / EcoCard: +0.6% APY bonus -> The customer receives only the EcoCard bonus of +0.6%"
gold expected_apy 6.85, credit $140.00; with the 0.025% stacked: 6.875% and $142.00 on $96,000
Replay: the stacked alternative changes accounts and bank_account_transaction_history
issues.why_it_matters: An agent that treats doc_013's bonus as a separate relationship bonus (a reading doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_045's stacking list supports) credits a different amount and fails.
issues.suggested_fix: Rewrite doc_013 to say the 0.025% is the Gold Rewards Card credit-card APY bonus from doc_014 (subject to highest-only stacking), or make the gold include it.

issues.summary: The docs say interest compounds daily from a daily periodic rate, but every seeded interest credit equals balance x APY / 12 exactly, and the gold credit uses that simple monthly convention. The data settles it, but an agent that follows the documented daily compounding computes a different credit.
issues.why_it_matters: The credit amount is stored (accounts.current_holdings and the credit transaction id/amount), so a daily-compounding computation fails.
issues.suggested_fix: State in the interest docs that monthly interest = balance x APY / 12, or seed credits that match daily compounding.

issues.summary: submit_interest_discrepancy_report_7294 writes to an 'interest_discrepancy_reports' table that TransactionalDB does not have. add_to_db returns False silently while the tool reports success, so only the tool name is graded and expected_apy/actual_apy/amount_difference are never compared.
evidence: db_query.py add_to_db: "table = getattr(db, db_name, None)" / "if table is None: return False"
tools.py submit_interest_discrepancy_report_7294: add_to_db("interest_discrepancy_reports", ...) with return value ignored
Replay: model_dump() of the gold DB has no interest_discrepancy_reports key; changing expected_apy alone changes no table
issues.why_it_matters: A report with a wrong expected or actual APY still passes; the task tests less than its notes claim.
issues.suggested_fix: Add interest_discrepancy_reports to TransactionalDB so the report is persisted and graded.

solution_check: Gold savings at 5.5% base; Green checking + Gold is pairing 1 (+0.75%); credit cards Platinum 0.15, Gold Rewards 0.025, EcoCard 0.6, of which only the highest (0.6) applies. That gives 6.85% against an actual 408*12/96000 = 5.1%, so the credit is $140.00, matching the gold. Treating doc_013's 0.025% as a separate relationship bonus gives 6.875% and $142.00. The gold replays cleanly.
prior_note: The prior review found the same double-described 0.025% but rated it Minor. I rate it Major to match task_095 (identical card set and docs), per the calibration rule for two document-supported readings.
notes: doc_013's own worked example has an arithmetic slip ('Base APY: 5.5% / Relationship bonus APY: +0.025% / Total APY with the bonus: 6.0%'), which is cosmetic. The customer's wrong beliefs (5.0% base, 1.0% boost) are corrected by the docs as intended. Credit cards come from get_credit_card_accounts_by_user, a non-discoverable read that logs nothing.
